positions.as_written: Assess generalised hypermobility formally rather than by impression, using the standard multi joint assessment.
Ask about family history, since hypermobility is often familial.
Ask about symptoms separately from findings, because the symptom is what decides whether anything follows.
Examine both knees and several other joints, since the pattern is what establishes generalised laxity.
Record knee hyperextension, which is usually present.
Record the patellar translation, which is commonly increased.
